prompts.design.brief.short: Help me write a design brief for [what we're making].
prompts.design.brief.detailed: Help me write a brief for [what we're making]. What I know: [description]. Sections: goal (what the viewer should do or feel), audience, key message in one phrase, required elements, constraints (size, format, colours, deadline), what definitely isn't wanted. Ask questions where information is missing.
prompts.design.brief.refine: Cut the brief to 5 lines so it can be read quickly.
prompts.design.brief.check: Here's my design, described: [description]. Does it meet the brief?
prompts.design.mood.detailed: Project: [project], audience: [audience]. Suggest 3 different visual moods. For each: 3 keywords, colours in words, type style (serif, sans serif, handwritten), the character of the images, what to avoid. Explain how the audience would likely read each.
prompts.design.mood.refine: Combine moods [number] and [number]: what would that look like?
prompts.design.mood.check: My choice: [description]. Is there any clash between the colours, type and topic?
prompts.design.composition.short: Suggest a composition for [what we're making] with these elements: [elements]
prompts.design.composition.detailed: I need to arrange these elements: [elements] on a [format and size]. Main message: [message]. Suggest 3 composition options in words: where each thing goes, what's largest, where the eye is led, how much white space. For each, when it works best.
prompts.design.composition.refine: Adapt option [number] to a vertical phone format.
prompts.design.composition.check: Here's my layout: [description]. Where will the viewer look first? Is that what I want?
prompts.design.palette.short: Suggest a 4–5 colour palette for [project], described in words.
prompts.design.palette.detailed: Suggest 2 palettes for [project] with a “[mood]” mood. Table: colour role (background, text, accent, secondary), description in words, an approximate HEX code. Explain which combinations to use for text so it reads well, and which colours shouldn't sit next to each other.
prompts.design.palette.refine: Some viewers can't easily tell red from green. Adjust the palette.
prompts.design.palette.check: My colours: [colours]. Is there enough contrast for small text?
prompts.design.poster.detailed: I need a poster for [event]. Audience: [audience]. Required information: [information]. Suggest 3 different ideas: main image, headline (up to 6 words), composition, colours, how to present the required info so it reads in 3 seconds. No clichés like a light bulb for ideas.
prompts.design.poster.refine: Make option [number] more restrained for a formal event.
prompts.design.poster.check: Here's the text on my poster: [text]. What can go?
prompts.design.infographic.short: How can I turn this data into an infographic? [data]
prompts.design.infographic.detailed: Help me plan an infographic on “[topic]”. Data: [data]. Source: [source]. Suggest: the main point in one phrase, the order of blocks from top to bottom, a visual type for each figure (bars, proportion, scale, icons), labels. Don't add data I haven't given you.
prompts.design.infographic.refine: There are too many figures. Which 3 should stay so the main point survives?
prompts.design.infographic.check: Does my chosen visual distort the proportions? [description]
prompts.design.hierarchy.short: Help me build a visual hierarchy: [elements]
prompts.design.hierarchy.detailed: The layout has: [elements]. What matters most to the viewer: [main point]. Rank the elements by importance (levels 1, 2, 3) and for each level suggest: size, weight, colour, spacing. Explain which hierarchy tools to use if everything is the same size.
prompts.design.hierarchy.refine: Right now everything is shouting at once. What should be quieter?
prompts.design.hierarchy.check: Here's the order I read my layout in: [order]. Does it match the intended order?
prompts.design.cover.short: Suggest cover ideas for a project on “[topic]”.
prompts.design.cover.detailed: I need a cover for a [type of work] on “[topic]”. Required: the title and [what else]. Suggest 4 ideas: image, title placement, colours, style (photo, illustration, type only, diagram). For each, the impression it gives and how hard it is to make yourself.
prompts.design.cover.refine: Make a version using only text and one simple shape.
prompts.design.cover.check: Is it clear from my cover what the work is about, without reading the subtitle? [description]
prompts.design.alt.short: Write alt text for this image: [image description]
prompts.design.alt.detailed: Help me write alt text. What's in the image: [image description]. Where it appears and why: [context]. Rules: up to 125 characters, the key point first, no “image of” or “picture of”, convey its meaning in the page's context. If it's purely decorative, say the alt should be empty.
prompts.design.alt.refine: It's a chart. How do I put the main finding in the alt and the full data in nearby text?
prompts.design.alt.check: My alt text: [text]. Would a screen-reader user understand why the image is there?
prompts.design.overloaded.short: My layout is overloaded: [description]. What should go?
prompts.design.overloaded.detailed: Here's an overloaded layout: [description]. Its purpose: [goal]. Suggest how to simplify: what to delete, combine or shrink, where to add white space, how many fonts and colours to keep. Give a list of changes in order, starting with the biggest effect.
prompts.design.overloaded.refine: I can't remove anything. How can I simplify using only layout and size?
prompts.design.overloaded.check: After the changes: [description]. Is it now clear what matters most?

verify.design.brief: Show the brief to the client or teacher before starting: it saves rework.
verify.design.mood: Test the mood with real people from the audience: show a sketch to two or three of them.
verify.design.composition: Check the composition on a small screen and from a distance: what catches the eye first?
verify.design.palette: Check text–background contrast with a free contrast checker: beautiful doesn't always mean readable.
verify.design.poster: Check every detail on the poster: date, time, place. Those are the mistakes people notice first.
verify.design.infographic: Check every figure on the infographic against its source and credit the source at the bottom.
verify.design.hierarchy: A simple test: squint at the layout. Whatever stands out is what reads as most important.
verify.design.cover: If you use someone else's photos or fonts, check the licence. For school work, credit the source.
verify.design.alt: Write alt text based on what's actually in the image. The AI can't see the picture if you've only described it.
verify.design.overloaded: When removing elements, check the required information is still there.
